synopsis: Scenario-language choice determines whether thousands of concrete tests can be generated, varied and traced automatically; the booklet recommends an open, manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled catalogue using Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy, exporting to OpenSCENARIO where required [f14493, f1606, f14491]. OpenSCENARIO XML 1.4.0 (2026) supports precise synchronized maneuvers, while DSL 2.2.0 (March 2026) supports abstract scenarios, parameter variation and performance indicators, but both retain road-traffic domain models [f13204, f13205, f13206]. OpenSCENARIO XML and OpenDRIVE have broad tool support, yet identified off-road gaps include deformable terrain, airborne particles, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation; extensions or a manufacturer domain model are therefore needed rather than abandoning OpenX [f8616, f14488, f7434]. Scenic 3 offers 3D geometry, occlusion-aware visibility and probabilistic placement without lanes, but is not an ISO or ASAM standard, leaving adopters responsible for requirements, rig and exchange-format mappings [f7174, f7177]. No single off-road scenario language covers the problem, and planning should not depend on an off-road standard arriving before mid-2027; existing EMESRT storyboards provide useful mining-hazard content but are not machine-readable [f7147, f7205, f7184].
